decisions.reason: As a close-to-core cardboard display variant that was publicly presented and fits the firm's quality-and-service strategy, management is likely to continue it and justify the earlier launch unless clear failure is undeniable.

This pegboard-backed display is still near the established offer, so the firm has some public and development commitment to defend, though its more specialized format makes discontinuation somewhat easier than for the most standard models.

A standard quarter-pallet cardboard display sits squarely in the firm's core business, making it easy for management to keep supporting it and frame any weak performance as temporary in a flat market.

The eighth-pallet format is a narrower niche, but because it remains part of the core display family and was visibly launched, escalation of commitment still makes continuation more likely than withdrawal.

The wooden display pallet extends beyond the firm's paper-centered core, so despite some commitment already made, management has less strategic justification to persist if results have not clearly validated the move by 2022.

Although this is a close-to-core quarter-pallet display, its specific focus on media products makes weak demand harder to explain away as temporary after several years, so management is more likely to cut it and reallocate capacity.
